Senses.Explanation: “Filial devotion is called the precepts” is wording explicitly quoted from the Brahma’s Net Sutra, not an anonymous Chan maxim. Yongjue Yuanxian contrasts filiality in the Buddha teaching with the Confucian duties he lists: material support, reverence, establishing one’s reputation, burial, and sacrifice; he then locates filiality in recognizing that the child's dharma-body is the parents' original body rather than stopping at those services. Zhuanyu Heng quotes the same scripture while arguing that filial devotion and keeping the precepts are not two commitments. Shiyu Mingfang directly applies the clause in a memorial address. In Hanyue Fazang’s record, an unnamed questioner raises the scriptural wording and Hanyue answers it. These Chan uses quote, explain, apply, or test one scriptural clause.

Senses.Explanation: In the Chan corpus this bird is overwhelmingly the goose king that selects milk from water. One instruction gives the image directly: 'there is milk in water; people do not see it; the goose king selects it.' Another says that when water and milk are mixed, the goose king eats the milk. Masters then use the fixed line 'the goose king selects the milk, naturally not of the duck kind' as an appraisal after cases and answers. In a hall exchange an unnamed monk asks the purport of that line and Fenyang Shanzhao answers, 'south of the river there is; north of the river there is not,' without explaining the bird further. Another address pairs capacities: it takes a goose king to select milk and a lion to bite. A verse also reverses the stock contrast: under one strike, 'the goose king becomes a duck; the soft-shelled turtle becomes a tortoise.' The Zen deviation is this legendary bird's repeated use—and deliberate reversal—as a teaching-seat appraisal of selection and discrimination; the entry does not add a hidden object beyond the milk, water, goose, and duck named by the records.

Occurrences.Kwic: 義解者謂。識是心家之識。心是識家之心。此二者如水乳難辨。當知識是水。心是水中之乳。所以教家謂。鵝王擇乳寧同鴨類。但是水中皆有乳。惟鵝王能辨。自餘水族皆莫之知。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0145.xml). Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben of Tianmu. Zhongfeng Mingben. Zhongfeng owns the explanatory prose while introducing the image as inherited teaching language.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「第一義諦，一椎粉碎了也。一粉碎後，便盡卻今時。盡卻今時，卻向那邊行履。那邊行履時，見天不是天，見地不是地，見山不是山，見水不是水。向那裡打個轉身，卻向這邊行履，見天依舊是天，見地依舊是地，見山依舊是山，見水依舊是水。正是溈山道：『這邊那邊，應用不缺。』大眾！且道作麼生甄別？」良久云：「鵝王擇乳，素非鴨類。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB192.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daxiu Zhu. Daxiu Zhu. Daxiu asks the discrimination question and supplies the capping phrase.

Senses.Explanation: The goose king separates out the milk names the traditional image of distinguishing milk from water. Zhongfeng Mingben explicitly sets water and milk side by side and says the goose king alone can distinguish them. Dahui Zonggao, Tianyin Yuanxiu, and Daxiu Zhu use the phrase, usually with 素非鴨類, as a verdict or answer when asking who can distinguish. The cited passages do not turn that comparison into a general faculty or doctrine.

AlternateTargets: the goose king separates milk from water, unlike a duck

Occurrences.Kwic: 如溈山問仰山云寂子今時人還假悟也無仰山曰悟則不無爭奈落在第二頭癡人面前不得說夢將謂是真箇仰山道悟則不無爭奈落在第二頭他自有出身路何故他是悟了底人方可恁麼說得所以溈山肯之曰如是如是這箇是鵝王擇乳素非鴨類如今人夢也未曾夢見也隨例說悟是第二頭悟是枝葉正是獅子咬人狂狗趂塊且從你說悟是第二頭只如溈山又道研窮至理以悟為則此語又如何消遣都來溈仰父子因甚麼作兩般說話你要信他落在第二頭即是信他以悟為

Senses.Explanation: “The goose king selects milk; it is never of the duck kind” credits discriminating recognition: a capable reader separates what is worth taking from what merely resembles it. Dahui Zonggao uses the verdict in two retained recorded-sayings witnesses to reject a superficial treatment of awakening or to cap a case.
